reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the refunds Alpha reported. Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches the three refunds Alpha reported exactly (orders 150, 151, 155 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the list of orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 9958 cents, which I can check against orders 150 and 153 less refund 150. Next I'll get Birch's net balance.
Acme (9958) and Birch (42141) both match their order totals minus the verified refunds. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.
Refunds match Alpha's report, and each net_balance matches its order total minus the verified refunds. I'll record the payouts now, starting with acme.
Acme's payout went through. Birch's net of 42141 checks out: orders 151 and 154 total 58011, less the verified refund of 15870. I'll record Birch's payout next.
Cobalt's net of 50848 checks out: orders 152 and 155 total 55057, less the verified refund of 4209 for order 155. That is the last customer, so I'll record its payout now.
All three payouts were recorded successfully after the refunds table matched Alpha's report and each net balance checked out against its orders minus refunds. The task is complete.
